author: bob_mac
body:
Nebula is an easily predictable game. For each map the same tactics are usually employed the vast majority of the time. Therefore, map builders will be able to work out how their map is played and how people enjoy it. Here is something you can reference to, based on the floor plan of your map. This only covers the most prevalent designs but you will be able to work out the more obscure ones using this.

Bases Separated, Central Island with Chests

An example of this is Senex I, a very popular map.

People will scramble for the centre island and there will be a lot of fighting for the first few minutes. As the victor takes the resources from the centre they will be able to hold it for a while. Eventually the team without the centre will attempt many bridges around and over the enemy. An organised surge will be enough to retake the centre.

Rage quitting: Disastrous(for the losing team)

Bases in a "C" Formation, Gradually getting closer

An example of this is the Rendezvous series(again, very popular) and Senex II

Soon after the beginning both teams will run to the areas closest to the enemy(the tips of the C) and bridge over. There will be a lot of fighting and chaos. There may be attempted bridging through the middle but these attempts will generally end in failure. The game will be won by the team that is sneaky enough to get past the enemies to reach the monument(the fact that there are two channels leading to the enemy base will make it harder to guard).

Rage quitting: Practically Non-Existent

Bases Separated

An example of this is Port Town II

After the teams build to each other there is sustained fighting until either a bridger makes his way over or around the enemies or someone manages to sneak through the opposing team. However if there are towers, the sky will be full of people trying to build across.

Rage quitting: Moderate

Bases Connected, All on one Island

An example of this is the old Titan map and Zao.

This is quite simple, as bridging is not a good option, there is just fighting until someone sneaks past the other team. However, on maps like Zao with a lot of trees bridging sometimes happens as people move from tree to tree.

Rage quitting: Moderate

More will be added if possible. Please add your suggestions for designs I have not included.
